hero.title: Master's in Computer Engineering in France for Indian Students
hero.subtitle: Advance your microelectronics and embedded systems mastery in France across elite Grandes Écoles and research universities, benefiting from Europe's Silicon Valley in Grenoble and up to 2 years of post-study stay-back under the Franco-Indian partnership.

overview: France is home to one of Europe's most significant microelectronics and semiconductor research clusters, notably centered around the European Silicon Valley in Grenoble and the aerospace engineering hubs of Toulouse. Studying a master's in Computer Engineering in France offers Indian students rigorous scientific training in nanoelectronics, embedded computing, and hardware acceleration.

French institutions offer English-taught 2-year Master of Science (MSc) and Diplôme d'Ingénieur degrees. Coursework provides deep specialization in Micro and Nano-Electronics, System-on-Chip (SoC) Design, Embedded Artificial Intelligence, Real-Time Systems, and Autonomous Robotics, incorporating mandatory 6-month master's research internships in advanced corporate research laboratories such as CEA-Leti and STMicroelectronics.

Upon completing a recognized Master's degree in France, Indian students can access post-study work authorization under the Carte de Séjour Recherche d'Emploi ou Création d'Entreprise (RECE). Supported by the Franco-Indian bilateral partnership on student mobility, Indian Master's alumni are eligible for up to a 2-year post-study stay-back period, providing ample time to launch careers as Semiconductor Engineers and Embedded Firmware Architects across Paris, Grenoble, and Lyon.

Eligibility criteria for computer engineering PG in France Normally applicants should have a bachelor's degree in a relevant subject, and adequate preparation in computing and mathematics. The common eligibility criteria for computer engineering PG in France include: A recognized Bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, information technology, electronics, electrical engineering or a related discipline. Outstanding academic results in relevant subject matter. Knowledge of programming, algorithms, data structures, computer architecture or mathematics as appropriate to the program. English language skills for programs delivered in English. French language skills for programs taught in French. Any other requirements imposed by the institution. For Indian applicants, a BTech, BE, BSc or equivalent degree may be acceptable, depending on the academic requirements for the program. A degree in an unrelated discipline may not adequately prepare someone for an advanced computing specialization.

sections.title: Why Study Computer Engineering PG in France?
sections.lead: Computer engineering  integrates computer hardware , software , digital systems , networks and computing architecture . France provides the chance to learn advanced technical skills in these areas via university master programmes and engineering-school education\.

items: Advanced technical specialisations: Develop expertise in embedded systems, artificial intelligence, computer architecture, cybersecurity, robotics, and distributed computing.
Research opportunities: Some programs have good contacts with research laboratories and collaborative projects.
Industry-oriented learning: Depending on the program, students may engage in technical projects, internships or co-op placements.
Programmes taught in English: Many institutions offer master's programs in English for international students.
Study in Europe: French qualifications are within the European higher education framework, depending on the degree and its recognition.
Further academic studies: A relevant master's degree can be a pathway to doctoral research, depending on the admission requirements.
Students should choose a program based on their preferred specialization, academic background, language of instruction and career objectives.

sections.title: Computer Engineering Postgraduate Courses in France
sections.lead: The title of each concerned French program may not contain the word "Computer Engineering". Applicants should also look for master's degrees in computer science, electronics, embedded systems and digital engineering\.

items: Typical specializations are:
Computer Engineering: Computer architecture, hardware/software integration, digital systems and computing platforms.
Computer Science: Algorithms, software engineering, operating systems, databases and distributed systems.
Embedded Systems: Firmware, IoT devices, real-time systems, microcontrollers.
Cybersecurity: Network security, cryptography, secure software and systems security.
Artificial Intelligence: Machine learning, data science, intelligent systems, deep learning.
Cloud Computing and Networks: Distributed systems, virtualization, network infrastructure, cloud platforms.
Robotics and Autonomous Systems: Control, perception, embedded computing, and automation.
Electronics and Digital Systems: Digital circuit design, signal processing, semiconductor technologies, hardware design.

A national Master's degree usually lasts for two years after a relevant Bachelor's degree and is worth 120 ECTS credits in the master's cycle. Some programs will accept applicants directly into year 2 if they have appropriate preparation at postgraduate level.

sections.title: Requirements for Admission
sections.lead: Applications to French universities and engineering schools are evaluated on the basis of the admissions criteria of each school.

items: Common admission requirements for postgraduate degrees in computer engineering in France are:
Certificate of Bachelor's degree or provisional certificate
Academic transcripts (official). - Curriculum Vitae (CV)
Statement of purpose (SOP) or letter of motivation.
English language test results, if applicable.
Proof of French language skills for courses taught in French.
Recommendation letters, if requested.
Passport or other accepted forms of ID.
Portfolio, programming projects or research experience for chosen programs.
Interview or technical evaluation as appropriate.
Some courses may require algorithms, programming languages, computer systems, electronics or advanced math as a prerequisite.

sections.title: Admission Process
sections.lead: The PG admission process for computer engineering in France depends on the university, course, nationality and present country of residence.

items: Pick a specialisation: Decide if you want to specialize in computer science, embedded systems, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence or some other computing field.
Shortlist programs: Compare curriculum, language of instruction, qualification, duration, fees and career opportunities.
Check the requirements: Make sure that your bachelor degree and previous subjects satisfy the entry requirements.
Identify the application platform: Depending on the program, applications may be submitted through the institution's portal, through Études en France, or on another platform.
Prepare your documents: Have your transcripts, certificates, CV, motivation letter and language test results ready.
Submit the application: Adhere to the official instructions and deadline.
Selection Process: Attend interviews or submit further technical documentation if required.
Accept the offer: Follow the instructions to enroll and arrange tuition payments.
Prepare for arrival: Complete any required student visa formalities and arrange for accommodation.

sections.title: Recognition and Accreditation
sections.lead: Students should check the degree awarded and its recognition status before enrolling.

items: A Master's degree is a degree in the French and European system of higher education. A Diplôme d'ingénieur is a separate qualification and its current authorization and accreditation should be checked with the Commission des titres d'ingénieur (CTI), where appropriate.
Check the following prior to applying:
The exact title of the degree and the institution that granted it.
Whether the degree is a national Master's or a engineering diploma.
Duration of the program and ECTS credits.
Current accreditation status, if applicable.
Internship and research possibilities.
Admission to doctoral study or to further professional education.

faqs.q: Can I do PG in computer engineering in France after BTech or BE?
faqs.a: Yes. A relevant BTech or BE can make you eligible to apply for a master's program in computer engineering, computer science, embedded systems or related fields. Entry is determined by your academic history and the programme's entry requirements.

faqs.q: What is the duration of PG in computer engineering in France?
faqs.a: A national Master's degree is usually two years after the relevant bachelor's degree. Some programs offer applicants who meet the advanced-entry criteria direct entry to second-year status

faqs.q: Can I do a PG in computer engineering in France in English?
faqs.a: Yes. Some institutes, such as Grenoble INP – Ensimag, offer master's programs in computer science and related disciplines taught in English.

faqs.q: What are the computer engineering PG tuition fees in France?
faqs.a: For 2026-2027, the public-university Master's reference fee is €255 per year for eligible French and EU students and €3,950 per year for non-EU students subject to differentiated fees. Different prices may apply for Specialized international programs and private institutions.

faqs.q: After doing PG in computer engineering in France, what kind of jobs can I get?
faqs.a: Depending on your specialization, career options may include software engineering, embedded systems, cybersecurity, cloud infrastructure, computer architecture, artificial intelligence, robotics, and research and development.
